question:
Fill in the blank with a suitable collective noun from the given options:

The police arrested the _____of thieves who were active in our area.
solution:
The correct answer is 'gang'.

Key Points

  • The collective noun for a group of thieves is a gang. 
    • Example - A gang of thieves on mopeds ran over a tourist whose watch they were trying to steal and broke his leg.
  • Hence, option 1 is the correct answer. 
     

Complete sentence - The police arrested the gang of thieves who were active in our area.

Additional Information

  • Crowd is used to describe a group of people.
  • Group is used to describe a collection of dancers, singers or performers. 
  • Mob is used to describe a large crowd of people.

question:
Choose the right/apt collective nouns from the alternatives given below each sentence and fill in the blanks :

A __________ of cattle was grazing in the forest.
options: More than one of the above
solution:
The correct answer is 'herd.'

Key Points

  • The fitting collective noun for 'cattle' is 'herd.'
  • Each collective noun corresponds with a certain group of objects or beings.
  • Cattle are typically grouped as a 'herd.'
  • A 'herd' is a large group of animals, especially hoofed mammals, that live, feed, or migrate together or are kept together as livestock.

Therefore, the completed sentence should read: "A herd of cattle was grazing in the forest."

Additional Information

  • 'Flock' (usually used for a group of birds)
  • 'Swarm' (used for a large or dense group of insects)

question:
Fill in the blanks with the CORRECT pronoun in the given sentence:

____ flowers are in the vase? ____ are lovely. ____ arranged them?
solution:
The correct answer is "Whose, They, Who".Key Points

  • The sentence requires the use of pronouns to fill in the blanks.
  • The first blank requires a possessive pronoun which indicates ownership.
  • "Whose" is the correct option as it is the possessive form of "who".
    • Example: Whose book is this? 
  • The second blank requires a subject pronoun to replace the noun "flowers".
    • Example: They are going to the park.
  • So, "they" is the correct option as it is the subject pronoun that refers to plural nouns.
  • The third blank requires an interrogative pronoun as the question mark indicates that the sentence asks a question.
  • So, "Who" is the correct pronoun for the third blank.
  • Putting all the pronouns together, the correct sentence is: "Whose flowers are in the vase? They are lovely. Who arranged them?"
  • Hence, option 4 is correct.

question:
Fill in the blank with the correct option.

This is ______ book and I am reading it now.
solution:
The correct option to fill in the blank is "None of the above".

Key Points

  • The word "my" indicates that the book belongs to the person speaking.
  • Here, the speaker is saying that "This is my book and I am reading it now."
  • The other options are incorrect as "hers" would indicate that the book belongs to a female, "mine" indicates that the book belongs to the speaker, "ours" indicates that the book belongs to a group of people, not just the speaker.
  • Thus, among the given options, none of the above is the correct answer.

question:
Directions: Complete the sentences with suitable alternatives:

You _______  to finish this on time because you have no choice.
options: More than one of the above
solution:
The correct answer is 'have.'

Key Points

  • "Have" indicates a necessity or obligation.
  • The context of having no choice emphasizes the requirement to finish on time.
    • Example: "You have to complete the assignment by tomorrow."
  • Grammatically correct as it aligns with the sense of a definite obligation.

Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 3'.

 Additional Information

  • Option 1: "may have" implies possibility, not necessity.
  • Option 2: "could have" implies a past possibility, inappropriate here.

question:
Directions: Fill in the blanks with the appropriate word:

I don't think I've ever _______ on that sofa.
options: More than one of the above
solution:
The correct answer is "sat".

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in the present perfect tense. Therefore the form of the verb should be in past participle form.
  • Let us explore the given options:
    • Been sitting is used in the present perfect continuous tense.
    • Sat is the past participle form of the verb.
    • Sit is the base form of the verb.
  • Hence, the correct answer is option 2.
     

Complete Sentence: I don't think I've ever sat on that sofa.

question:
Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. 

None of our team members is faster than Nikhila. She is our ______ athlete.
options: More than one of the above
solution:
The correct answer is 'fastest.'

Key Points 

  • If the superlative degree (Shalini is our tallest player among the friends) says about the best thing then the rule is:-
    • For comparative, use -
    • None of ...... + be verb + adjective/adverb(comp. form) + than + Subject
      • Example: None of the friends is taller than Shalini
  • ​​The given question consists of two sentences.
  • The first sentence follows the pattern of a sentence in the comparative degree and the second sentence must follow the pattern of a superlative degree.
  • Now the word 'fast' has one syllable. 
  • We usually add –est to a one-syllable word to make a superlative degree.
  • The superlative degree of the adjective "fast" is "fastest."
  • The given sentence compares the speed of Nikita with all the team members and mentions that she is the best among them.
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 3.
     

Correct sentence: None of our team members is faster than Nikhila. She is our fastest athlete. 

Additional Information   

  • The positive degree of an adjective is its simple form.
  • It is used to denote the mere existence of some quality.
  • Adjectives in the positive degree are used when no comparison is made.
  • The degree of comparison of an adjective describes the relational value of one thing with something in another clause of a sentence.

question:
Directions: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

He is ______ poorer than all his friends.
solution:
The correct answer is 'much.'

Key Points

  • The given sentence talking about someone's level of poverty.
  • Therefore, the most appropriate word to be filled in the blank is 'much'.
  • The word 'much' means very. 
    • Example: This command has a much richer set of options and arguments than a lookup function.
  • 'Much' is often used with comparative adjectives and adverbs: much older, much faster.
  • We can use 'much' before comparative adjectives and adverbs to make a stronger comparison.
    • Example: Sometimes the prices in the local shop are much better than the supermarket's prices.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Complete Sentence: He is much poorer than all his friends.
 Additional Information

  • Let us explore  the other options:
    • 'Most' means greatest in number or amount. (संख्‍या या मात्रा में अधिकतम)
    • 'More' means to a greater degree than usual or than something else. (सामान्‍य या अन्‍य से अपेक्षाकृत अधिक)
    • 'Very' means extremely; in a high degree. (अत्‍यधिक, बहुत; बड़ी मात्रा में)
       

Hinglish

  • दिया गया वाक्य किसी के गरीबी के स्तर के बारे में बात कर रहा है।
  • इसलिए, रिक्त स्थान की पूर्ति के लिए सर्वाधिक उपयुक्त शब्द 'much' है।
  • 'Much' शब्द का अर्थ अत्‍यधिक है।
    • उदाहरण: This command has a much richer set of options and arguments than a lookup function.
  • 'Much' अक्सर तुलनात्मक विशेषणों और क्रियाविशेषणों के साथ प्रयोग किया जाता है: much older, much faster.
  • हम तुलनात्मक विशेषणों और क्रियाविशेषणों से पहले 'much' का उपयोग एक मजबूत तुलना करने के लिए कर सकते हैं।
    • उदाहरण: Sometimes the prices in the local shop are much better than the supermarket's prices.


अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 1 है।

पूर्ण वाक्य: He is much poorer than all his friends.

question:
Select the most appropriate adverb to fill in the blank.

Vikas Khanna is a master chef. He cooks ________.
options: More than one of the above
solution:
The correct answer is "delightfully".

Key Points

  • In this sentence, we need an adverb that describes the manner in which Vikas Khanna, a master chef, cooks.
  • So, the appropriate choice is "delightfully".
  • "Delightfully" suggests that the action of cooking is performed in a manner that brings joy or pleasure.
  • Given that Vikas Khanna is described as a master chef, it is logical to assume that his cooking would be characterized by producing delightful results, both in terms of the process and the final dishes.

Therefore, the correct answer is "option 2".

question:
Directions: Fill in the blanks in the following sentences with the correct alternative.

He is nothing else in my house ________ a liability.
options: More than one of the above
solution:
The correct answer is, 'but.'
Key Points
  • The correct option to fill in the blank is, 'but.'
  • The adverb 'else' is followed by 'but' and 'rather' is followed by 'than.'​
    • Example: He was doing nothing else but eating.
  • ​In the given sentence, else is used thus we need to use but as its pair.

​The correct sentence is: He is nothing else in my house but a liability.
Additional Information

  • The adverb 'yet' is used to denote 'up to the moment of time' and it is used in negative or interrogative sentences.
  • It is generally used with present perfect tense and not with the past tense. 
    • Example: The postman has not come yet.

​​

  • रिक्त स्थान को भरने का सही विकल्प है, 'but'
  • adverb 'else' के बाद 'but' और 'rather' के बाद 'than' आता है।
    • ​Example: He was doing nothing else but eating.
  • दिए गए वाक्य में, else का प्रकार प्रयोग किया जाता है  इसके  लिए जोड़ी के रूप में but की जरूरत है।
  • adverb 'yet' का उपयोग 'समय के इस क्षण तक' को दर्शाने के लिए किया जाता है और इसका उपयोग negative या interrogative वाक्यों में किया जाता है।
  • यह आम तौर पर present perfect tense के साथ प्रयोग किया जाता है और past tense के साथ नहीं।
    • Example: The postman has not come yet.

question:
Directions: Each of the following sentences in this section has a blank space with four options. Select whichever preposition or determiner you consider the most appropriate for the blank space and indicate your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

You have to leave your shoes ______ the door when you enter the house.
options: More than one of the above
solution:
The correct answer is 'by.'

Key Points  

  • Let us see the meanings of the given prepositions​:
    • By: We use "by" to mean ‘beside’ or ‘at the side of’.
      • Example: There’s a lovely café by the river. 
    • In: We use "in" when something is located inside of a defined space.
    • It could be a flat space, like a yard, or three-dimensional space, like a box, house, or car.
    • The space does not need to be closed on all sides.
      • Example: I can see emotions in her eyes.
    • "Over" means above or higher than something else, sometimes so that one thing covers the other; above.
      • Example: Helicopters dropped leaflets over the city.
    • "To" is a preposition which is used to indicate a goal or a direction of movement, as well as a place of arrival.
      • Example: That's the way you use it when you say you're going to class tomorrow.
  • ​​The sentence refers that the person had to leave his shoes beside the door, so the correct answer is "by" for it.
  • ​Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
    ​

Correct sentence: You have to leave your shoes by the door when you enter the house.

question:
Directions: In this section, each of the following sentences has a blank space and each sentence is followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill the blank space.

__________ his parent's disapproval, he joined this university.
solution:
The correct answer is "Despite ".

Key Points

  • The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is "Despite".
  • The word "despite" is a preposition which is used to introduce a notion that something occurred even though there was a factor that might have prevented it from happening.
  • In this case, "despite" denotes that he joined the university even though his parents disapproved.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 2".

Complete Sentence: Despite his parent's disapproval, he joined this university.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank

The monster was a strange creature _______ it was made entirely of steel.
options: More than one of the above
solution:
The correct answer is 'because'.

Key Points

  • Let's discuss the marked option; i.e. 'because':
    • Because: used to introduce a clause that gives the reason of what has been said or done
      • Ex: She spoke quietly because she didn’t want Catherine to hear. ('because' introduces the clause containing reason of why she spoke quietly)
  • In the given sentence, a monster was described as a strange creature and an additional clause describes the reason why it is a strange creature.
  • Hence, 'because' is the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is option 2).

Complete sentence: The monster was a strange creature because it was made entirely of steel.

Additional Information

  • In case:  to talk about things we should do in order to be prepared for possible future situations
    • Ex: In case I forget later, here are the keys to the garage.
  • So: to introduce clauses of result or decision
    • Ex: It was a long journey, so I’m really tired now.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The food was well cooked ________ bland.
options: More than one of the above
solution:
The correct answer is 'but'.
 
Key Points
  • The word "but" is used as a conjunction to introduce a contrast or an exception to what has just been stated.
  • In this context, it introduces a contrast between the food being well-cooked and being bland.
  • The contrast here is between the positive aspect of the food being well-cooked and the negative aspect of it being bland.
  • "But" effectively connects these contrasting ideas.
  • Using "than" (option 1), "so" (option 2), or "or" (option 3) would not be grammatically correct in this context, as they do not convey a sense of contrast between the two qualities of the food.

​Therefore, the correct answer is ‘Option 3.

Complete Sentence: "The food was well cooked but bland."
 
Additional Information
  • "Than" is used in comparisons and does not apply here as there is no comparative structure in the sentence.
  • "So" is used to introduce a result, which does not fit the context of expressing a contrast between two qualities.

question:
Choose an appropriate word from the options to suitably fill the blank in the sentence below so that the sentence makes sense, both grammatically and contextually.

To create awareness and building an entrepreneurial environment, a lot of emphasis ____________ now be given to create infrastructure for mentoring startups.
solution:
The correct answer is 'should'.

Key Points

  • The correct word to use in this context is 'should', which indicates a recommendation or necessary action.
    • Would implies a conditional action, which is not suitable here.
    • Could indicates possibility but lacks the sense of recommendation.
    • Shall is too formal and not commonly used in modern contexts.
    • Will indicates a future action but does not carry the sense of recommendation.
  • Therefore, 'should' is the most appropriate choice to complete the sentence.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: To create awareness and build an entrepreneurial environment, a lot of emphasis should now be given to create infrastructure for mentoring startups.

Additional Information

  • When choosing a modal verb, it is important to consider the context and the recommendation or necessity it conveys.
    • Example: Students should complete their homework on time.
  • In sentences involving recommendations or necessary actions, 'should' is typically the correct modal verb to use.
    • Example: Employees should follow the company's guidelines.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I am sure that my seeds ______ by next week.
options: More than one of the above
solution:
The correct answer is 'will grow'.

Key Points

  • The most appropriate option for the given blank is 'will grow'.
  • In the given sentence 'next week' is an adverb of 'future simple tense'.
  • Other adverbs of 'future simple tense' are 'tomorrow, today, later today, in five minutes, in two hours, on Monday, on Saturday afternoon, next week/month, this year, etc.'
    • Example: Bob will go to the library tomorrow.
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 3.
     

Correct Sentence: I am sure that my seeds will grow by next week.

Hinglish

  • दिए गए रिक्त स्थान के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त विकल्प 'will grow' है।
  • दिए गए वाक्य में 'next week' 'future simple tense' का adverb है।
  • 'future simple tense' के अन्य adverbs हैं 'tomorrow, today, later today, in five minutes, in two hours, on Monday, on Saturday afternoon, next week/month, this year, etc.'।
    • Example: Bob will go to the library tomorrow.
  • अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 है।

question:
Direction: Fill in the blanks with the correct option.

She was very courageous to learn to _______ ski at fifty.
options: No Article
More than one of the above
solution:
The correct answer is 'No article.'

Key Points 

  • In the given sentence, the word "ski" is used as a verb.
  • The meaning of "ski" is to move over snow on skis. (स्‍की बाँधकर बर्फ़ पर चलना)
  • Articles (a, an and the) are used before nouns or noun equivalents and are a type of adjective.
  • Articles are not used before a verb.
  • So, we don't need any article in the blank.
  • Hence, the correct answer is Option 2.
    ​

​Correct sentence: She was very courageous to learn to ski at fifty.

question:
Fill in the blank with the suitable article:

I met ___ old man in the train.
solution:
The correct answer is 'an'. 

Key Points

  • The most appropriate article to fill in the given blanks is 'an'. 
  • If any word starts with the vowels or has any vowel sound then the article 'an' is used before them. In the given sentence 'old' starts with a 'vowel'.  
  • Example: 
    • The exam lasted hour and a half.
    • The exam lasted an hour and a half.
  • ‘A’ or ‘an’ are sometimes used in the vague sense of the certain, it means that we only have some basic information about the person and it is not enough to make it a certain object.
  • Here we only know that the person was old and since it starts with a vowel sound, ‘an’ is the best fit.    
  • ​​Therefore, by reading the above explanation we find that the correct answer is Option 3. 
    ​

Correct Sentence: I met an old man in the train.

  • दिए गए रिक्त स्थान को भरने के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त article 'an' है।
  • यदि कोई भी शब्द vowels से शुरू होता है या कोई vowel sound से शुरू होता है तो 'an' का उपयोग किया जाता है। दिए गए वाक्य में 'old' 'vowel' से शुरू होता है।
  • Example: 
    • The exam lasted hour and a half.
    • The exam lasted an hour and a half.
  • 'A' या 'an' कभी-कभी कुछ के अस्पष्ट अर्थ में उपयोग किया जाता है, इसका मतलब है कि हमारे पास केवल व्यक्ति के बारे में कुछ बुनियादी जानकारी है और यह एक निश्चित वस्तु बनाने के लिए पर्याप्त नहीं है।
  • यहां हम केवल यह जानते हैं कि वह व्यक्ति बूढ़ा था और चूंकि यह एक स्वर से शुरू होता है, इसलिए 'an' ’सबसे उपयुक्त है।
  • इसलिए, उपरोक्त स्पष्टीकरण को पढ़कर हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर विकल्प 3 है।

 

सही वाक्य:I met an old man in the train.

question:
Direction: The sentence given with the blank is to be filled with an appropriate word. Four alternatives are suggested for each question. Choose the correct alternative.

The peasantry ________ the most vulnerable to climate change impacts.
options: More than one of the above
solution:
The correct answer is 'are'.

Key Points

  • According to subject-verb agreement, a singular subject takes a singular verb and a plural subject takes a plural verb.
    • Example: Ram goes to the temple every day.
      ​                 She is one of the best artists who have ever lived.
  • There are certain nouns that are singular in form but plural in meaning. Such nouns must take a plural verb.
    • cattle, poultry, peasantry, children, gentry, police, people, cavalry, infantry, etc.
    • Example: The police have caught the thieves.
  • The given sentence is a general fact and so, it should be in the simple present tense.
  • Thus, 'are' is the correct answer.


Complete sentence: The peasantry are the most vulnerable to climate change impacts.

Additional Information

  • 'Have' means 'to possess, own or hold'. It is used with plural subjects.
    • Example: They have a big bungalow.
  • It can also be used as a helping verb in the present tense. 
    • Example: I have completed my homework.

  • Subject-verb agreement के अनुसार, एकवचन subject एकवचन क्रिया लेता है और बहुवचन subject बहुवचन क्रिया लेता है।
  • उदाहरण: Ram goes to the temple every day.
    ​              She is one of the best artists who have ever lived.
  • कुछ संज्ञाएं हैं जो रूप में एकवचन हैं लेकिन अर्थ में बहुवचन हैं। ऐसी संज्ञाओं को एक बहुवचन क्रिया लेनी चाहिए।
    • cattle, poultry, peasantry, children, gentry, police, people, cavalry, infantry, etc.
      मवेशी, घरेलू मुर्गियां, किसान, बच्चे, उच्च श्रेणी के लोग, पुलिस, लोग, घुड़सवार सेना, पैदल सेना, आदि।
    • उदाहरण: The police have caught the thieves.

question:
Fill in the blank with most appropriate tense:
When I was a child, I ___ to the park every evening.
solution:
The correct answer is 'used to go'.
 
Key Points
  • The phrase "used to go" is the correct form to describe a habitual action in the past.
  • The sentence is referring to an action repeatedly performed in the past ("when I was a child").
  • Option 1: "use to go" is incorrect because "use" does not agree with the past tense.
  • Option 3: "use to went" is incorrect because "went" is a past tense and cannot follow "use to."
  • Option 4: "was going" is incorrect because it describes a continuous action, not a habitual one.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
 
Complete Sentence: "When I was a child, I used to go to the park every evening."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "use to go" is incorrect because the word "use" must change to "used" to match the past tense.
  • Option 3: "use to went" is incorrect because "went" cannot follow "use to" in proper grammar.
  • Option 4: "was going" is incorrect because it implies a continuous action rather than a habitual one.
